To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the generalization gap can be bounded in terms of the Information Bottlenequilibrium and the mutual information between the data and the representation; (b) the generalization ability can be improved by minimizing a suitable combination of this bound and the empirical risk.

1) The information bottleneck objective can be derived as an upper bound to a cross-entropy based objective; 2) The information bottleneck can help to decrease the cross-entropy based generalization gap, thus improving the generalization ability; 3) Dropout can be seen as a regularizer that helps to minimize this gap.

(i) the generalization gap can be upper bounded by the difference between the cross entropy of the empirical distribution and the true distribution, and (ii) the Information Bottleneck principle provides a theoretical explanation for why noise injection at the representation level can help improve generalization.
